name: Parties and Effective Date
text: This Real Estate Option Agreement is made and entered into the ist day of August 2006 (‘Effective Date”), by and between 1200 6" Street LLC,("Optionor”), a Limited Liability Company, whose address is 16630 Southfield Road, Allen Park, Michigan, 48101 and the United States of America, acting by and through the U.S. General Services Administration (‘Optionee”) whose address is 230 S. Dearborn Street, Suite 3600, Chicago, Illinois, 60604.

name: 1. Grant of Option
text: 1. Grant of Option. The Optionor hereby grants to the Optionee the exclusive and irrevocable option (‘Option’) to purchase certain real property situated in the City of Detroit, County of Wayne, State of Michigan containing approximately 10.89 acres which is commonly known as 1200 6" Street (“Property”) and is more particularly described in the Agreement for Purchase and Sale of Real Property which is attached hereto and made a part hereof as Exhibit 1, together with all improvements, easements, and appurtenances to the Property for the price and within the time specified in this Option.

name: 1. Assignability
text: This Option shall be fully assignable at any time prior to closing to Optionee’s developer (“Developer”).

name: Section 2 — Term and Exercise of Option
text: 2. Term of Option. This Option shall continue in effect for a period of not less than one (1) year from the Effective Date of this Option and may be exercised in accordance with its terms at any time on or before its expiration inclusive of any extension period provided for herein, by serving written notice on the Optionor in the manner prescribed in Section 20.

name: 2. Extension of Option
text: This Option may be extended at the election of Optionee for an additional thirty (30) days by giving notice as provided in Section 20 of this Option.

name: 3. Purchase Price
text: 3. Purchase Price. The total purchase price for the Property shall be $9,000,000 (Nine Million Dollars), hereinafter the “Purchase Price".

name: 3. Payment at Closing
text: At the closing on the Property (“Closing”), the sum of $8,000,000 (Eight Million Dollars) shall be due and payable plus or minus any standard deductions and prorations (Customary closing expenses incurred by the Optionor inclusive of utility and real estate tax prorations).

name: 3. Outstanding Balance Payment Rate
text: The remaining balance less any deductions identified below shall be paid at a rate of 10% of the annual tax incremental financing reimbursement received by Developer.

name: 3. Outstanding Balance Payment Example
text: For example, the anticipated annual Tax Incremental Financing [TIF] amount is approximately $2,000,000, of which an estimated $200,000 shall be paid to Optionor annually, and shall become due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt of same until the remaining $1,000,000 (or less, dependent upon deductions as described below) are received (‘Outstanding Balance”).

name: 3. Interest on Outstanding Balance
text: The Outstanding Balance shall accrue interest to the same extent, if any, that either the City of Detroit or the State of Michigan pay interest to the Developer on the outstanding incurred eligible expenses and which shall be paid in accordance with Exhibit 1.

name: 3. Tax Incremental Reimbursement
text: In the event the sale is consummated, and subject to repayment of the Outstanding Balance owed to Optionor (less any deductions) the tax incrementa! reimbursement shall belong to the Developer.

name: 4. Conveyance
text: 4. Conveyance. Upon payment of the Purchase Price, less the Outstanding Balance, Optionor shall convey good and marketable indefeasible fee simple title to the Property to the Developer by warranty deed, free and clear of all liens and encumbrances whatsoever, subject only to those items (‘Permitted Exceptions”) set forth in Exhibit 1, and subject to any standard deductions, prorations and or adjustments as provided for herein.

name: 5. Survey Delivery
text: 5. Survey. No later than thirty (30) days after the effective date of this Option, the Optionor shall deliver to Optionee, at Optionor’s expense, a topographical metes and bounds land title survey of the Property in accordance with the 2005 Minimum Standard Detail Requirements for ALTA/ACSM Land Title Surveys including such Table A items as Optionee may elect,

name: 5. Survey as Exhibit 2
text: the same shall be attached hereto and made a part hereof as Exhibit 2.

name: 5. Updated Survey
text: Optionor shall provide Optionee an updated topographical boundary survey of the Property which shall reflect the City of Detroit’s final approved plat of vacation and or dedication of right of way necessary to affect the Optionee’s desired street closures by December 31, 2006.

name: 5. Description of Contiguous Properties
text: Additionally, the updated topographical boundary survey shall describe all of the immediate contiguous properties created as a result of vacating Sixth Street and Abbott Street for the purpose of combining the Property as a single metes and bounds legal description that shall be identified as one (1) tax parcel.

name: 5. Surveyor’s Certificate
text: The surveyor’s certificate shall be certified to the Developer’s title company so that the Owner’s Title Insurance Policy for the Property that will be obtained by the Developer at closing will contain a survey endorsement based on the final topographical boundary survey and plat.

name: 6. Title Commitment
text: 6 Title Insurance. No later than thirty (30) days after the effective date of this Option, the Optionor shall deliver to Optionee, at Optionor’s expense, a Preliminary Title Commitment for an Owner’s Title Insurance Policy to issue to Optionee or its Assignee, at or as soon as possible after Closing, its ALTA Form B Owner's title insurance policy, without standard exceptions, in the amount of the purchase price, insuring title to the Property to be in good and marketable condition, free and clear of any liens and encumbrances.

name: 6. Commitment Documents
text: Seller shall furnish Purchaser with the aforesaid title commitment and legible copies of all items shown in such commitment as soon as possible, but in no event later than thirty (30) days following the Effective Date.

name: 6. Notice of Title Defects
text: If the title is not in the condition required hereunder, Optionee shall notify Optionor in writing of such defect(s) within twenty-one (21) days after receipt of the title insurance commitment and copies of all items shown therein.

name: 6. Remedies for Title Defects
text: In the event Optionor is unable or unwilling to cure such defects within twenty-one (21) days after receipt of such notice, Optionee shall have the option of either (1) waiving such defect(s) and proceeding with the closing; (2) allow Optionor to attempt to resolve the exceptions and encumbrances objected by Optionee, during the term of the Option, such as in the case of those encumbrances which will require the action of the City of Detroit; or (3) if the defect can be cured by the payment of dollars, deducting the amount required to cure such defect from the purchase price and the proceeds due Optionor at Closing or, at Optionor's discretion, the obtaining by Optionor of a surety bond over such lien or title defect.

name: 6. Permitted Exceptions
text: Those title conditions not objected to by Optionee pursuant to this . paragraph or accepted by Optionee are hereinafter called “Permitted Exceptions.”

name: 7(a). Ownership and Authority
text: 7, Optionor’s Representations. Optionor represents that: (a) It is the record owner of the Property and has the requisite power and authority to enter into and fully carry out this Option and the sale of the Property contemplated herein.

name: 7(b). Development, Possession, and Title
text: (b) It has no knowledge of any reason why the local governmental authorities would not allow the Property to be developed for the Federal office facilities contemplated herein; that possession of the land has been peaceable and undisturbed; that Optionor’s title to the Property has never been disputed or questioned to its knowledge; nor does Optionor know of any facts by reason of which said possession or title might be disturbed or questioned, or by reason of which any claim to the Property, or any part thereof might arise or be set up adverse to Optionor.

name: 7(c). Utilities
text: (c) Electricity, telephone, sewer, and water utilities have been installed within the adjacent public right of ways and are of sufficient size, capacity and are available for immediate connection at the Property without any special charge, assessment or apparatus for its current use.

name: 7(d). Facility Disclosure
text: (d) Optionor has disclosed that the property is a “facility” as defined by MCL 324.20101 et seq. due to the property’s historic uses described in the environmental reports Optionor provided to Optionee.

name: 7(d). Environmental Information
text: Optionor also represents that it has provided all environmental information that it has with respect to the environmental condition of the Property including the existence of asbestos containing materials located in existing structures.

name: 7(e). Environmental Compliance Representations
text: (e) Except as otherwise indicated on Schedule A attached hereto, or as described in paragraph 7 (d) of this agreement, to the best of Optionor’s actual knowledge: (1) that since Optionor acquired an interest in the property, Optionor has been in compliance with all federal, state and local laws, rules, regulations, ordinances, codes and orders governing, establishing, limiting or otherwise affecting the discharge or disposal of hazardous substances or hazardous waste; (2) that the property has not been used since the time Optionor acquired any interest in the property for storage, disposal, deposit, treatment, or recycling of toxic, dangerous or hazardous substances; (3) that in the event that any subsequent purchaser of the property avails itself of the available statutory exemptions from environmental liability, there are no activities on the property which would subject an owner thereof to damages, penalties, injunctive relief or clean-up costs under any federal, state or local law or under any civil action respecting hazardous substances on the property. The exemptions include that owner's obligations to comply with its due care requirements as stated in MCL 324.20107a, its obtaining a Baseline Environmental Site Assessment under MCL 324.20101 et seq. and compliance with the All Appropriate Inquiry exemption as defined and contained in CERCLA, as amended.

name: 7. Continuing Representations and Warranties
text: Optionor represents and warrants to the Optionee that the above representations are true and correct as of the date hereof and will continue to be true and correct on each day hereafter until and including any exercise of this Option.

name: 8. Phase II Assessment Results
text: 8. Due Care Activities. Optionee shall provide Optionor with the results of the Phase II Environmental Site Assessment being conducted by Wight & Company (‘Phase II) for the purpose of estimating the total costs of due care activities referenced in MCL 324.20107a (hereinafter referred to as “Due Care” activities) for inclusion in the Brownfield Plans as “Eligible Activities” as defined by State of Michigan’s Act 381 of 1996, as amended.

name: 8. Eligible Activities Cost Estimate
text: It is the responsibility of the Optionee to estimate the appropriate costs for the Eligible Activities.

name: 8. Cooperation on Due Care Activities
text: The parties shall reasonably cooperate in the determination of the most cost effective and appropriate Due Care activities to help ensure that those costs are approvable by the appropriate governmental authorities.

name: 8. Best Efforts for Reimbursable Costs
text: To this extent, the parties shall use their best efforts to obtain the maximum allowable reimbursable costs for the Eligible Activities.

name: 8. Limitation of Liability
text: In the event the governmental authorities do not approve all of the costs and activities necessary to achieve Due Care both during pre and post construction of the proposed federal facility, then Optionor shall be responsible for the unapproved amount not to exceed $500,000 (Five Hundred Thousand Dollars) (“Limitation of Liability”).

name: 8. Deduction from Outstanding Balance
text: The actual amount, up to the Limitation of Liability, shall be deducted from the Outstanding Balance due to Optionor.

name: 9. Closing Deadline
text: 9. Closing Date. The Closing on the Property shall be no later than 90 days after exercise of this Option by Optionee or its Developer.

name: 9. Closing Location
text: The Closing shall take place at the location provided in the attached Agreement for Purchase and Sale of the Property.

name: 10. Delivery of Possession
text: 10. Possession. Possession of the Property shall be delivered to the Optionee or its assignee on the date of Closing, unless a different possession date is agreed to between the parties.

name: 10. Inspection and As-Is Condition
text: Optionee will have an opportunity to inspect the Property and that the Property will be conveyed in “as is” condition except as otherwise provided for in the Option Agreement and the Agreement for Purchase and Sale of the Property.

name: 11. Right to Enter and Inspect
text: 11. Optionee's Right to Enter and Inspect the Property. The Optionee’s authorized or designated representatives or agents, or offerors participating in the lease procurement process of the Optionee, shall have the right during the period of this Option including any extension periods subject to the rights, interests, and uses made of the Property by the Optionor, to enter upon the Property for the purpose of inspecting same and making test borings, plans, topographical and boundary surveys, environmental assessments, and any other due diligence matters deemed reasonably prudent in connection with the contemplated use of the Property as a leasehold for Federal facilities.

name: 11. Insurance for Entrants
text: Optionee shall require any of said parties to maintain insurance in amounts and coverages reasonably acceptable to Optionor.

name: 11. Repair and Restoration
text: Said parties shall promptly repair and restore the Property to the same condition as existed immediately prior to such entry if such entry resulted in any damage thereto.

name: 11. Notice Before Entry
text: Optionee shall provide Optionor reasonable notice prior to entering the Property.

name: 12. Required Government Approvals
text: 12.__ Government Approvals. Optionor and Optionee acknowledge that the Property requires governmental approvals for Optionee’s intended use which may include, but not be limited to: governmental approvals of what is known as a Brownfield Plan (“BP”); street vacations; utility relocation; rezoning; site plan approval; special use permit; and variances.

name: 12. Optionor Approval Responsibilities
text: Optionor shall be responsible, at Optionor’s expense, for acquiring the necessary governmental approvals to affect vacations of Sixth Street and Abbott Street, and any zoning variances.

name: 12. Commencement of Street Vacations
text: Immediately upon the effective date of this Option, Optionor shall commence the process of vacating Sixth Street and Abbott Street and removing any encumbrances to title objected to by Optionee.

name: 12. Street Vacation Application
text: Optionor shall make application with the City of Detroit within thirty (30) days of the effective date of this Option for said street vacations.

name: 12. Public Road Land Costs
text: The parties shall as soon as practical determine whether any land must be acquired at a cost to the parties to relocate or construct any other public roads.

name: 12. Termination for Unallocated Road Costs
text: In the event that said costs will be required and the parties cannot agree to the allocation of those costs within sixty (60) days of a final determination of those costs, then Optionee may terminate this Option.

name: 12. Traffic Engineering Study
text: In the event that the City of Detroit requires Optionor to retain a certified traffic consultant to prepare a traffic engineering study as part of its required submittal to affect the City of Detroit's approval for those street vacations described above, then Optionor shall cause the preparation of such a study to occur.

name: 12. Traffic Study Costs
text: Optionor shall bear all costs for any traffic studies necessary to obtain the vacation of Sixth Street and Abbott Street and/or dedication of alternative public right of ways,

name: 12. Traffic Study Reimbursement
text: except that in the event Developer does not execute the Purchase and Sale Agreement identified in the Option and purchase the Site, then Optionee will use its best efforts to secure funds to reimburse Optionor for reasonable documented expenses to obtain such traffic studies (attorney's fees excluded), in an amount not to exceed $50,000.

name: 12. Support for Government Approvals
text: Optionor agrees to provide its support and written consent when required so as to allow Optionee the ability to seek and obtain any and all necessary governmental approvals prior to closing.

name: 12. Consultation and Approval
text: Prior to closing on the Property, Optionor shall consult with Optionee and shall obtain Optionee’s written approval when Optionor is obtaining any governmental approvals on the Optionee’s behalf that affect the Property.

name: 12. Drafting Brownfield Plan
text: Immediately upon execution of the Option, Optionor shall commence drafting the Brownfield Plan and other documents required by the governmental! authorities with the cooperation and assistance of Optionee.

name: 12. Eligible Activities List
text: Optionee shall determine and supply the list of “Eligible Activities” with the assistance of the Optionor, and their estimated costs associated for the Eligible Activities that Optionee desires to include in the Brownfield Plan.

name: 12. Reasonableness of Estimated Costs
text: The costs, while estimated, must be reasonable and necessary to affect Optionee’s intended use.

name: 12. Approval of Draft Brownfield Plans
text: Optionor shall submit all draft Brownfield Plans to Optionee for written approval prior to their submittal to the City of Detroit and/or the State of Michigan.

name: 12. Brownfield Plan Approval Deadline
text: After Optionee has provided such written approval, Optionor shall take all steps necessary to obtain approval of the Brownfield Plan for the project prior to Optionee by no later than December 1, 2006.

name: 12. Extension of Brownfield Deadline
text: This deadline may be extended by the Optionor for four (4) additional thirty (30) day periods so long as the delays are not caused by the Optionor.

name: 12. Deduction for Unapproved Eligible Costs
text: In the event that the City of Detroit approves an amount less than the agreed upon costs for Eligible Activities, that amount (up to the Limitation of Liability) shall be deducted from the Outstanding Balance.

name: 12. Brownfield Process Liability Exclusion
text: In no event shall the Optionor be responsible for the failure of Optionee or Developer to comply with the Brownfield process or for any shortfalls in anticipated reimbursement due to the fault of either Optionee or its Developer.

name: 12. Reimbursable Costs
text: Any costs or expenses which may or will be reimbursed pursuant to State of Michigan’s Act 381 shall be the responsibility of Optionee or its Developer.

name: 12. Retention of Outstanding Balance
text: In the event that the Brownfield Plan has not been approved prior to Closing, the Outstanding Balance shall be retained by Optionee until such time as the necessary governmental approvals are obtained.

name: 13. Assignment Without Consent
text: 13. Assignment; Disclosure. This Option may be assigned by the Optionee, without the consent of the Optionor.

name: 13. Assignment Documents
text: The Optionee shall provide the Optionor with a copy of the fully executed assignment instrument prior to any closing of sale under this Option and a copy of Exhibit 1, executed by the Developer.

name: 13. Further Assignment
text: This Option shall be subject to further assignment only with the prior written consent of the original Optionee.

name: 13. Developer Evaluation
text: The Optionee shall’ make any and all evaluations it deems necessary in it sole discretion as to the financial ability or condition of the Developer to proceed with a project for the construction and lease of Federal office and related facilities contemplated for the Property.

name: 14. Failure to Exercise Option
text: 14. Failure to Exercise Option. If Optionee elects not to exercise the rights, option, or fee simple interests granted herein and to complete the purchase within the time and in the manner provided herein, then this Option shall terminate without further action or obligation on the part of either party.

name: 15. No Partnership or Agency
text: 15. Parties. Nothing contained in this Option shall constitute the parties hereto as partners with one another or agents for one another,

name: 15. Gender and Number
text: As the context may indicate, any term used herein shall include the singular, plural, ferninine, masculine or neuter gender, as the case may be.

name: 15. Construction of Herein Terms
text: The words “herein”, “hereunder” and “hereof” and other equivalent words refer to this Option as an entirety and not solely to the particular portion I which such word is used, except if otherwise expressly limited.

name: 16. Additional Instruments and Acts
text: 16. Additional Documents. Optionee and the Optionor shall each execute and deliver any other additional instruments and documents, and do all acts as may be necessary to implement and effectuate the intent of this Option and to carry out the general purpose of the Option;

name: 16. Recordable Releases and Corrections
text: and each shall upon the request of the other, join in any instrument or document in recordable form as may be necessary to release rights hereunder should this Option terminate or otherwise, to correct the public records.

name: 16. Form of Documents
text: All such documents shall be in the form and substance satisfactory to the parties and their respective counsel.

name: 17. Counterparts
text: 17. Counterparts. This Option may be executed in any number of counterparts, any one of which shall be considered an original, and all of which, taken together shall be deemed to be one original.

name: 18. Entire Agreement and Supersession
text: 18. Prior Agreements. The parties agree and acknowledge that this Option cancels and supersedes all prior agreements, whether written, oral, or both; is entire in itself; and that this Option, Exhibit 1, and a Memorandum of Option (Exhibit 3) executed on the same date as this Option are the only agreements between the parties hereto respecting the Option and the Property; that all agreements and undertakings between the parties are embodied in this Option and Exhibit 1.

name: 18. No Other Inducements
text: No promises, covenants, or representations of any kind, other than those expressly contained herein or in Exhibit 1, have been made to induce any party hereto to enter into this Option.

name: 18. Amendments
text: This Option may be amended only by written instrument executed by Optionee and Optionor.

name: 19. Contract Disputes Act
text: 19. Disputes. This contract is subject to the Contract Disputes Act of 1978 (41 U.S.C. sections 601-613) (‘Act’).

name: 19. Resolution of Disputes
text: Except as provided in the Act, all disputes arising under or relating to this Option shall be resolved under this Act.

name: 19. Contracting Officer
text: The Contracting Officer for purposes of this Option shall be Mr. Forrest Hudson, General Services Administration, Region 5, Office of Property Development.

name: Section 20 — Notices
text: 20. Notices. All notices or communications required under this Option or which either party desires to give to the other shall be sent by certified or registered, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, United States mail, personal delivery, or recognized, private, overnight courier which maintains evidence of delivery and in the case of a notice or communication to the Optionee, is addressed as follows: General Services Administration, Attn: Mr. Forrest Hudson, Office of Property Development, 230 S.-Dearborn Street, Suite 3600, Chicago, Illinois, 60604; and in the case of a notice or communication to the Optionor, is addressed as follows; Mr. Sam Danou, 1200 6" Street LLC, 16630 Southfield Road, Allen Park, MI, 48101, or is addressed in such other way as the parties may from time to time direct by written notice to the other.

name: 21. Time of the Essence
text: 21. Time of the Essence. Optionor and Optionee mutually agree that time is of the essence throughout the term of this Agreement and every provision hereof in which time is an element.

name: 21. Separate Extensions of Time
text: No extension of time for performance of any obligations or acts shall be deemed an extension of time for performance of any other obligations or acts.

name: 21. Nonbusiness Day Performance
text: If any date for performance of any terms, conditions or provisions hereof shall fall on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, then the time of such performance shall be extended to the next business day thereafter.

name: 22. Evidence of Optionor Authority
text: 22. Authority of Optionor. Concurrently with the execution of this Option, Optionor shall furnish to the Optionee a certified copy of the resolution, or if the Optionor is a general or limited partnership, the written approval of the general partner(s) authorizing the Optionor to consummate this transaction together with a certified copy of the partnership or limited partnership agreement.

name: 22. Additional Authority Instruments
text: The Optionor shall further provide such other instruments as the Optionee shall deem appropriate in its reasonable judgment to evidence the authority of the Optionor to consummate this transaction.

name: Exhibit 3 — Parties and Effective Date
text: This Memorandum of Real Estate Option Agreement (Memorandum of Option Agreement”) is made and entered into the 1% day of August 2006 (“Effective Date”), by and between 1200 6™ Street LLC,(Optionor”), a Limited Liability Company, whose address is 16630 Southfield Road, Allen Park, Michigan, 48101 and the United States of America, acting by and through the U.S. General Services Administration (‘Optionee”) whose address is 230 S, Dearborn Street, Suite 3600, Chicago, Illinois, 60604.

name: Exhibit 3 §1. Grant of Option
text: 1. Grant of Option. In accordance with the Real Estate Option Agreement between the Optionor and Optionee dated August 1, 2006, Optionor granted to the Optionee the exclusive and irrevocable option (‘Option’) to purchase certain real property situated in the City of Detroit, County of Wayne, State of Michigan containing 10.89 acres which is commonly known as 1200 6" Street (“Property”) and is more particularly described in Attachment A attached hereto and made a part hereof, together with all improvements, easements,.and appurtenances to the Property for the price and within the time specified in this Option.

name: Exhibit 3 §1. Assignability
text: This Option is fully assignable at any time prior to closing to Optionee’s developer (“Developer”).

name: Exhibit 3 §2. Term and Exercise
text: 2. Term of Option. This Option shall continue in effect for a period of not less than one (1) year from the Effective Date of this Option and may be exercised in accordance with its terms at any time on or before its expiration inclusive of any extension period provided for herein, by serving written notice on the Optionor in the manner prescribed in Section 20 of the Real Estate Option Agreement.

name: Exhibit 3 §2. Effect of Exercise Notice
text: The giving of such notice shall result in Exhibit 1 of the Real Estate Option Agreement becoming a binding contract of purchase and sale between the parties, effective on the date of the receipt of notice of exercise of the Option as provided in said Section 20.

name: Exhibit 3 §2. Extension
text: The Option may be extended at the election of Optionee for an additional thirty (30) days by giving notice as provided in Section 20 of the Real Estate Option Agreement.

name: Exhibit 3 §3. Purpose of Memorandum
text: 3. PURPOSE OF MEMORANDUM OF OPTION AGREEMENT. This Memorandum of Real Estate Option Agreement is prepared for the purpose of recording to give public notice that the Optionee or its assignee has the right to purchase the Property.
